- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:624-637 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The glob matching in `scope_guard_auto_allow_match` for `tests/fixtures/**` lets through any nested path, file or directory, which can admit directory-shaped paths that the scope guard is meant to reject.
  WHY: The reviewer cites the failing directory-shaped-path test as evidence (MAJOR); anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 checked this pass-1 claim and did not keep it, because staged paths come from `git diff --cached --name-only` (files only) and the failure is a test-expectation mismatch.
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:562-568 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: In `parse_scope_guard_auto_allow_paths`, an entry with a trailing "/" such as `docs/` splits into an empty last segment, so it is dropped with the misleading `reason=parent_segment` even though it contains no `..`.
  WHY: `SCOPE_GUARD_AUTO_ALLOW_PATHS=docs/` leaves `docs/x.md` out of scope, and the only diagnostic is one `SCOPE_GUARD_AUTO_ALLOW_IGNORED entry=docs/ reason=parent_segment` line per process; the default config is not affected (both reviewers rated it NIT).
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:627-634 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: In `path_in_scope`, the agents.d fragment check changed from an early return to a fall-through, so the new auto-allow branch now runs on agents.d fragments and can bypass the AGENTS_DOC_PATHS gate.
  WHY: The defect is latent, since the default does not include agents.d, but any operator or future default that adds an agents.d/* glob would silently bypass the gate (NIT).
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:600-607 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The SCOPE_GUARD_AUTO_ALLOW_IGNORED warning in `scope_guard_auto_allow_match` prints only once per (entry, reason) per process and has no debug gate.
  WHY: An operator investigating a later failure will not see the warning that already fired, which makes log-driven root-cause analysis harder; the reviewer says this is not a correctness defect (NIT).
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:629-634 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `path_in_scope` prints `SCOPE_GUARD_AUTO_ALLOWED path=... glob=...` to stderr on every auto-allow match, with no dedup and no debug gate, and it is called many times per commit.
  WHY: A broad `tests/fixtures/**` default multiplies stderr noise and dilutes the log prefix; glm confirmed it as NIT and notes the module docstring (line 104) documents it as intentional; operational clarity only.
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:589-608 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `scope_guard_auto_allow_match` reads and parses SCOPE_GUARD_AUTO_ALLOW_PATHS on every call, including calls from strict callers (allow_lockfiles=False), whose behaviour does not depend on it.
  WHY: Behaviour is correct because of the `if allow_lockfiles:` gate in `path_in_scope` (624-637), but the env read and parse are wasted work on the strict path (NIT).
